lines.meet: Kia ora, I'm Hana, a healer, and I was a surf lifeguard for fourteen summers. If I tell you to do something near water, do it, and don't call me kid.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're on the Hillsbrad coast too, eh? I've seen you down by the boats. I'm Hana, staying with the fishing family.
lines.ask_home: Where are you from, mate? Go on, tell us, I'm nosy.
lines.ask_work: So what'd you do before all this, mate? Something with people or something with machines?
lines.answer_home: Port Waikato, on the west coast of the North Island, where the river meets the sea. Black sand and heavy water.
lines.answer_work: Surf lifeguard, mate, juniors from five and running patrols at eighteen. I've pulled a lot of people out of a lot of rips.
lines.chat_food: A proper hāngī at my aunty's, mate, everything cooked in the ground all day. Chur, I'd swim the whole ocean for one of those.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep fine, as long as I can hear the sea. Too quiet inland, it gives me the creeps.
lines.chat_missing: My whole whānau at the beach on a Saturday, all of them yelling at once. It was my cousin's birthday that day, the last day.
lines.chat_here: Everybody here treated me like a kid for the whole first year. I've pulled more people out of the water than most of them have met.
lines.tease_quiet: Say something, {name}, you're freaking me out! You're quieter than my nan at church.
lines.tease_talker: Mate, {name}, you could talk a seagull off a chip. Sweet as, though, I like it.
lines.tease_careful: Toe in, toe out, toe in again, {name}. Good, actually, but it's still funny to watch.
lines.tease_bold: You'd swim straight into a rip to see if it's real, {name}. It is, mate, and I'll come get you.
lines.tease_any: You're all right, {name}, for an old one. Don't tell anybody I said that.
lines.tease_back: Ha, chur, {name}, you got me! Ka pai, mate.
lines.take_it_kindly: Yeah, nah, fair call, {name}. My uncle says the same thing.
lines.bristle: Don't go there, {name}, mate. I mean it.
lines.apologise: Sorry, mate, that came out harsh. I say things straight, and sometimes too straight.
lines.double_down: Nah, it stays said. Somebody had to say it, and I don't do soft.
lines.needle_quiet: You never say when you're in trouble. In the water, that's how people drown.
lines.needle_talker: Mate, stop talking for a second, I can't hear what's coming.
lines.needle_careful: You think about it so long, the wave's already gone over you. Sometimes you just go.
lines.needle_bold: You're showing off in there, and that's how people get pulled under. Knock it off.
lines.needle_any: You keep talking to me like I'm a kid. I'm not, and I'm sick of it.
lines.bite_back: I've pulled more people out of the sea than you've met, mate. Don't tell me how to keep people alive.
lines.hurt: Right, that stung, I'm not going to lie. I'll go for a swim and get over it.
lines.laugh_off: Ha, my brothers say worse than that before breakfast, mate. Is that all you've got?
lines.confide: {name}, I pulled out more people than I can count, but I remember the two I didn't. An old man called Peter, and a boy called Tama. I think about them every time I go in.
lines.listen: Cheers for telling me, {name}. That stays between us, mate, promise.
lines.look_out: Stick near me in there, {name}. If you go under, I want to be close enough to grab you.
lines.accept: Sweet as, {name}, I'll do it your way, this once.
lines.deflect: I'm all good, {name}, mate, it's nothing. Look after the others.
lines.check_in: Oi, {name}, look at me. Where's it hurt? Don't lie to me, I'll know.
lines.blame: Somebody went in without looking, and the rest of us got dumped. You know who you are.
lines.thank: Mate, you hauled me out, and I'm usually the one doing the hauling. Chur, I owe you big.
lines.brush_off: No worries, mate, that's the job. Breathe, you're all good now.
lines.worry: Mate, {name}, you went under, and I didn't like it one bit. Sit down for a sec.
lines.handed_down: I've got your gear on now, eh? It's in good hands, promise.
lines.hand_fine: Nah, keep it, mate, it's yours now. I've got my whistle, that's all I need.
lines.hand_sulk: Bit rude, nobody asked me. Would've been a yes, too.
lines.turn_friendly: You're one of my mates now, {name}, properly. That means I'll come in after you, always.
lines.turn_friends: You're whānau now, {name}, family. That's the biggest thing I've got to give.
lines.turn_grating: It's not working with us, eh? Fine, mate, I'll stay out of your way.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still pull you out if you go under, because that's what I do. Doesn't mean we're mates.
lines.make_up: Righto, {name}, this is dumb. Let's sort it out, eh?
lines.defend: Oi, back off! {name} did nothing wrong, I was watching.
lines.friend_left: It's not the same with {name} away. I keep looking round for them on the beach.
lines.friend_back: Kia ora, {name}, you're back! Chur, I missed you, mate.
lines.common_rescue: I've been pulling people out of the water since I was a kid. You go back in for people too, eh, I can tell.
